findings.evidence_quote: Lemma all_pairs_comm_nil comm : all_pairs_comm_sorted comm [::] = true.
findings.explanation: Stage 1 flagged the declaration line (442). Upgrading with closeness-to-target analysis: the name has four underscore-separated lowercase components (all, pairs, comm, nil). The `_nil` condition suffix is recognizable and appears in MathComp (e.g., `perm_nil`, `path_nil`), but the base `all_pairs_comm` is itself a three-component compound, making the full name unwieldy. MathComp grammar expects a single main symbol plus one or two canonical suffixes; a compound predicate name should be aliased so the lemma name remains two or three components: e.g., if `all_pairs_comm_sorted` were aliased as `pairwise_comm`, the lemma would become `pairwise_comm_nil` — two components with an idiomatic condition suffix.
findings.fix_sketch: Introduce a shorter alias for `all_pairs_comm_sorted` (e.g., `pairwise_comm`) and rename this lemma to `pairwise_comm_nil` or `pairwise_comm0`. If renaming the predicate is out of scope, add a `Naming:` line in the comment justifying the compound name.

findings.evidence_quote: Lemma subseqs_k_size k s t : t \in subseqs_k k s -> size t = k.
findings.explanation: The conclusion is `size t = k`, so `size` is the head symbol of the right-hand side and MathComp convention places it as a prefix: the canonical form is `size_subseqs_k`. The current suffix `_size` is descriptive but is not a single-letter entry in the AUTHORITY.md suffix table and inverts the standard prefix order used throughout MathComp (e.g., `size_cat`, `size_map`, `size_filter`). The statement is an equational result (`= k`), so an `E` suffix would also be acceptable: `subseqs_k_sizeE`, but the prefix form is more idiomatic when the main symbol is `size`.
findings.fix_sketch: Rename to `size_subseqs_k` following `mainSymbol_suffixes` grammar where `size` is the head of the conclusion, consistent with `size_cat` and `size_map`. Alternatively, if `subseqs_k` is the main symbol, use the canonical equational suffix: `subseqs_k_sizeE`.
